1/20/26: Re: Flock Raven Notification Leads to Arrest

On January 18th at 11:25 PM, officers from Uniform Patrol Shift 3 and the Evidence Response Unit received a
Flock Raven gunshot detection notification coming from the 1100 block of West 4th Street. The Flock Raven
system contains a series of devices placed throughout the City of Michigan City that are designed to detect the
sound of gunshots and the approximate location they originate from. This information is then immediately relayed
to officers so they can quickly respond to the scene.

Responding officers encountered 19-year-old Michigan City resident Terrion Wright upon their arrival. Officers
followed Wrights footprints that were left in the fresh snow cover before locating a spent ammunition cartridge and
loaded firearm within his path of travel. A closer inspection of the firearm revealed a conversion device was
attached to it which is commonly referred to as a switch. This device modified the semi-automatic firearm into a
fully automatic weapon known as a machine gun.

Wright was taken into custody for Operating a Loaded Machine Gun (Level 4 Felony) and Criminal Recklessness
with a Deadly Weapon (Level 6 Felony). The LaPorte County Prosecutors Office and LaPorte County Superior
Court 1 Judge Jaime Oss found probable cause to charge Wright with Operating a Loaded Machine Gun (Level 4
Felony) and Criminal Recklessness with a Deadly Weapon (Level 6 Felony). He was issued a $20,000 bond and his
booking photo is attached to this press release, courtesy of the LaPorte County Jail.

3/25/24: On March 23rd, 2024 at approximately 1:50 PM is when Officer Lewis received a notification from the citys Flock Falcon Camera System that a 2015 white Toyota Sienna with a California license plate had entered the city limits of Michigan City that was suspected in multiple out of state felony financial crimes. Officer Lewis quickly located this vehicle and conducted a traffic stop on it near the intersection of East US Highway 12 and East Michigan Boulevard.
The male driver produced a counterfeit identification card to Officer Lewis and was eventually identified as 32-year-old Washington state resident Florin Vaduva. Florin was arrested during the traffic stop for Possession of a False Government Identification (A-Misdemeanor). A female passenger was then identified as 26-year-old Washington state resident Loredana Vaduva. Loredana was arrested for 9 out of state felony theft warrants from Colorado, Minnesota and Wisconsin. Both Florin and Loredana were eventually transported to theLaPorte County Jail.
Officer Lewis learned during his investigation that Florin and Loredana were members of a nationwide criminal organization who are suspected of placing illegal electronic devices on automated teller machines (ATMs) known as skimmers. These devices are used to fraudulently record bank card data such as the card holders name, bank card number, expiration date, and bank card security code when a bank card is placed into an ATM. Florin and Loredana are also suspected of multiple illegal large-scale operations that defrauded several financial institutions across the country in excess of $500,000. Florin was identified as one of the high-ranking members within this criminal organization.
Probable cause was found by LaPorte County Superior Court Four Judge Greta Friedman on March 25th, 2024 to charge Florin with Possession of a False Government Identification (A-Misdemeanor). He was issued a$1,500 cash only bond and has since paid that amount to be released from the LaPorte County Jail. Loredana is currently awaiting extradition back to Colorado, Minnesota and Wisconsin. Both Florin and Loredanas arrest photos are attached to this press release courtesy of the LaPorte County Jail. The citys Flock Falcon Safety Camera and Raven gunshot detection systems have aided in the arrests of numerous offenders, solved a plethora of investigations, increased response times and continues to benefit the City of Michigan City in combating crime.

On May 31, 2023, at approximately 11:23 am, the Rantoul Police Department was alerted by Flock ALPR cameras of a vehicle associated with a missing person. Further investigation indicated the vehicle was believed to be involved with a parental abduction from Shelby County, Tennessee. Officers were able to locate the vehicle in the 700 block of West Champaign Ave., Rantoul. Officers located the occupants of the vehicle, one adult female and two juveniles, and learned one of the juveniles was reported as missing/endangered to the Memphis, TN police department on the morning of 05/31/23.

Upon further investigation, Shirley L. Webb, a 27-year-old female from Memphis Tennessee was arrested on a Shelby County, Tennessee Arrest Warrant for the offense of Felony Custodial Interference. Webb was later transported to the Champaign County Jail. Both juveniles were taken into protective custody until the custodial parent arrived, at which time they were reunited with family.

On November 7, 2022 at approximately 00:51 hours, the Rantoul Police Department was dispatched for multiple reports of shots heard in the area of the 800 block of St. Andrews Circle, Rantoul. Witnesses reported seeing a white SUV leaving the area at a high rate of speed after the reported shots. At approximately 01:13 hours, while officers were still checking the area, a resident in the 800 block of St. Andrews Circle called to report his residence had been struck by gunfire. Officers located evidence, including shell casings, in the area of the victims apartment.

Rantoul police officers searched images from nearby Flock Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs) and located a possible suspect vehicle. Using this Flock ALPR information, officers located the suspect vehicle, heavily damaged, in the 1400 block of Harper Dr., Rantoul. Visible inside the damaged vehicle was an AR-15 style rifle.

At approximately 02:00 hours, Rantoul police officers were advised a subject had been brought to a local hospital Emergency Department, via private vehicle, with injuries from a vehicle accident. Investigation revealed this subject was affiliated with the vehicle that was observed on the Flock ALPR, and was later located in the 1400 blk of Harper Dr.

As a result of the investigation, Rantoul Police arrested two individuals for weapon-related offenses.


On October 1, 2022, at approximately 6:15 PM, Flock ALPRS alerted officers to a possible stolen vehicle within the Village of Rantoul. Officers located this vehicle and confirmed it had been in fact reported stolen from Urbana, Illinois. As a result of this alert, one adult was arrested for the offense of Possession of a Stolen Vehicle.


On September 26, 2022, at approximately 11:47 AM, officers were alerted to a possible stolen vehicle entering the village of Rantoul by Flock ALPRs. Officers were able to locate this vehicle within the Village of Rantoul and confirmed this as a stolen vehicle from Champaign, Illinois. At 11:52 AM, officers successfully stopped this vehicle and one subject was taken into custody and transported to the Champaign County Jail for the offense of Possession of a Stolen Motor Vehicle.


On July 25, 2022, an arrest was made in connection to a homicide that occurred in Rantoul on April 12, 2022. Rantoul Police Detectives used Flock ALPR images to identify a vehicle possibly involved in the homicide. Using this information, detectives were able to confirm the identity of a suspect. After additional follow-up and interviews, a warrant was obtained for the suspect, who was later taken into custody without incident.


On May 24, 2022, the Rantoul Fire Department and Rantoul Police Department responded to a structure fire in the 1600 block of Gleason Dr. This was the third fire reported at this residence, which was already uninhabitable due to the previous two fires. All of these fires were deemed suspicious in nature. Rantoul Police Detectives were able to identify a possible suspect in these arsons. Detectives were able to locate Flock ALPR images of a rental vehicle which had been rented by the suspect, in the area of the fire and at the same time frame as the fire. The suspect, who is not from the area, was ultimately arrested for multiple arsons in the Champaign County area over a period of months.


On 06/17/22 Rantoul Officers took a report of a home invasion in which the suspect had already fled the scene. Rantoul officers obtained vehicle information for the suspect and entered the information into a Custom Hotlist on the Flock safety portal. On 06/20/22, the suspect vehicle passed by one of RPDs Flock cameras, activating the Hotlist alert. Based on this Hotlist alert, Rantoul officers were able to locate the suspect vehicle and arrest the suspect for the previous home invasion.


On 6/14/2022, Officers used the Flock ALPR system to search for a vehicle reported stolen the previous evening. Officers located a recent image of the stolen vehicle on a Flock camera and were able to locate the vehicle nearby. As a result, an offender was located and arrested, and the vehicle was returned to its owner.
san-jose-ca-pd:
On June 3, 2024, AIR3 was notified of a Flock stolen vehicle hit. AIR3 located and followed the suspect vehicle until it parked. AIR3 put out updates as patrol responded and the driver abandoned the vehicle. AIR3 guided in patrol units ten minutes later to the suspects location and took him into custody.

On June 4, 2024, AIR3 was notified of a Flock stolen vehicle hit. AIR3 located the suspect vehicle parked behind a power relay station. AIR3 saw two male suspects approach the vehicle and one of the suspects got into the drivers seat. AIR3 put out the information and confirmed the vehicle was stolen. AIR3 saw the suspect move the truck roughly forty feet where they tried to jump start a red Ford sedan. Patrol officers arrived on scene and arrested the driver.

On June 6, 2024, AIR3 responded to a Flock hit for a Ford pickup truck. Patrol Officers located the vehicle near the highway and AIR3 immediately responded to the location. Patrol Officers initiated an enforcement stop on the stolen vehicle and it immediately fled at a high rate of speed. AIR3 took over tracking the vehicle and advised patrol of the vehicles location and direction of travel. The driver ghost rode the truck as he fled on foot from the vehicle. AIR3 guided patrol units to the suspect who ran approximately one block after abandoning the vehicle. The suspect was taken into custody and booked into Santa Clara County Main Jail.

On July 3, 2024, officers responded after receiving a report of potential explosive device(s) being placed outside an office building. Arriving officers located a suspicious device. The primary building and a neighboring building were safely evacuated. Bomb Squad members responded to the scene and effectively rendered the device safe. The Assaults Unit and MERGE Unit began actively following up on leads and identified a suspect vehicle via Flock and a possible suspect. The MERGE Unit located the suspect vehicle and apprehended the suspect at a retail business in the area. The suspect was booked into Santa Clara County Main Jail for several crimes including possession of a destructive device.

On July 5, 2024, officers responded to a strong armed robbery incident at a retail chain store. Officers collected evidence at the scene, including a license plate for the suspect vehicle and surveillance footage. The suspect vehicle was located unoccupied near the possible suspect's residence. Flock ALPR cameras were utilized throughout the investigation. The suspect and his female getaway driver were located a short distance from the suspect's residence while they were walking towards another unassociated vehicle. They were both taken into custody without incident. A subsequent probation search at the residence yielded additional evidence. The suspect was positively identified by the victim and both suspects were booked into jail for multiple felony crimes.

On July 13, 2024, an officer utilized the Flock camera system to locate an occupied stolen vehicle. The suspects drove into a residential neighborhood where they abandoned the vehicle and fled on foot. One juvenile was apprehended during a foot pursuit. Officers nearby responded and set up containment around the yards the two remaining suspects were last seen. A drone was used to locate one suspect hiding in a backyard. During an attempt to call out the suspect he fled into an adjacent backyard and was arrested without incident. The driver was identified and booked into Santa Clara County Main Jail for possession of a stolen vehicle, resisting arrest, and possession of pepper spray by a felon.

On April 10, AIR 3 and officers from the Street Crimes Unit responded to a Flock hit for a felony vehicle that was wanted for evading Fremont PD the previous evening. The vehicle was found parked unoccupied in a department store parking lot. The suspect and passenger exited the building and entered the vehicle. A vehicle stop was attempted but the suspect vehicle fled at a high rate of speed. The vehicle later pulled over to released the passenger and proceeded to flee again. Patrol officers did not pursue, however AIR 3 continued to track the vehicle. The vehicle got onto the highway where it collided with several vehicles before being disabled. The suspect fled on foot and was later taken into custody without incident by patrol officers. The vehicle was confirmed to be stolen. The suspect was booked for PRCS violation, misdemeanor narcotics charge, evading police, and eight counts of assault with a deadly weapon.

On May 15, AIR3 located a stolen vehicle via Flock system. As the Aircrew started broadcasting the suspects location, SCCSO deputies got behind the vehicle and initiated a vehicle stop. Aircrew switched to the SOs channel and took control of the stop, directing operations from the sky. As additional units were arriving on scene, the driver fled from the vehicle on foot. He was quickly apprehended with the assistance of an SO K9 and taken into custody.

On May 23, AIR3 was notified of a stolen vehicle via Flock system. AIR3 located the stolen vehicle and a patrol unit initiated a vehicle stop. The suspect vehicle fled at a high rate of speed. Patrol officers did not pursue and instead tracked the vehicle at a distance. AIR3 continued calling the locations for several minutes until the vehicle parked in a gas station parking lot. The driver ran from the vehicle on foot. AIR3 guided patrol units to the suspect's location where he was taken into custody.

On May 27, AIR3 got a Flock hit for a stolen vehicle. AIR3 followed the suspect vehicle until it parked at a convenience store. Patrol units moved in and initiated a vehicle stop. Officers took two suspects into custody. One suspect was on active probation and was booked into jail.

On March 17, the department helicopter, AIR 3, responded to a Flock alert for a stolen vehicle. AIR 3 located the vehicle parked at a 7-11 and then saw the suspect driver exit the 7-11 and enter the vehicle. AIR 3 tracked the vehicle until patrol officers caught up to it. Officers performed a vehicle stop and took the suspect into custody without incident. The suspect also had a warrant out of Santa Clara PD.

On March 25, patrol officers located a stolen vehicle after being alerted by the Flock system. Upon attempting to stop the stolen vehicle, the vehicle fled at a high rate of speed. Officers did not pursue the vehicle but utilized the assistance of the department helicopter, AIR 3, to keep a visual of the vehicles direction of travel. The suspect ultimately abandoned the stolen vehicle and fled on foot. The suspect then flagged down a passerby for a ride and entered their car. Officers conducted a vehicle stop on the passerby and the suspect fled on foot again. After a short foot pursuit, the suspect was taken into custody without incident. The suspect was booked into jail for possession of a stolen vehicle and evading arrest.

On February 3, the department helicopter, AIR 3, responded to a Flock alert of a stolen truck. AIR 3 located the vehicle unoccupied and parked. Later, two female suspects entered the vehicle and drove away from the parking lot. Patrol officers initiated a vehicle stop on the suspect vehicle, but the vehicle fled. Officers did not pursue. AIR 3 continued to monitor the suspect vehicle which was later involved in a motor vehicle collision. The two female suspects fled on foot from the scene but were detained by nearby arriving officers. The driver was booked into the county jail for multiple felony charges including possession of a stolen vehicle, evading, hit and run, and probation violation. The passenger was booked for possession of stolen property and narcotics charges.

On February 5, the department helicopter, AIR 3, responded to a Flock alert for a felony vehicle that was wanted for evading. AIR 3 located the vehicle and tracked it until it parked in a residential neighborhood. Officers attempted an enforcement stop on the vehicle and the suspect fled on foot. Officers pursued on foot and eventually took the suspect into custody after a physical struggle. During the foot pursuit, the suspect tossed a Glock handgun onto the roof of the nearby residence before being taken into custody. The firearm was recovered and determined to be reported lost out of a neighboring jurisdiction. The Suspect also had a felony No Bail warrant for violating the terms of his Post Release Community Supervision (PRCS). The Suspect was booked into jail for multiple on-view gun charges, felony identity theft and violently resisting arrest.

On February 7, the department helicopter, AIR 3, located a stolen vehicle after receiving a Flock alert. The suspect vehicle parked under a townhouse carport and the driver fled on foot before units arrived on-scene. The suspect then shed clothing and hid under a carport at a neighboring complex. AIR 3 guided patrol units to the suspects location. Upon contact, the suspect ran away and was taken into custody after a brief foot pursuit. The Suspect was found to have multiple felony and misdemeanor warrants for possessing stolen vehicles, robbery, and brandishing a weapon. The suspect was booked into the county jail for possession of a stolen vehicle, resisting arrest and his outstanding warrants.

On January 3, the Department helicopter, AIR 3, responded to a Flock hit on a wanted felony vehicle. The vehicle had a seizure warrant for evading a police officer, and for lost/stolen plates. The suspect exited the vehicle and entered a restaurant in a shopping center. AIR 3 crew broadcasted the suspects description and patrol officers arrived on scene and apprehended the suspect. The suspect had two outstanding felony warrants and the vehicle was determined to have been reported stolen.

On January 11, the Department helicopter, AIR 3, responded to a Flock hit for a reported stolen vehicle. AIR 3 located the stolen vehicle getting onto the freeway and confirmed the vehicle was outstanding. The stolen vehicle came to a stop in a parking lot and the suspect walked away toward the back of a building./The helicopter guided patrol officers to the car and then to the suspect who was hiding behind an electrical box. Patrol officers took the suspect into custody and arrested him for the stolen vehicle, possession of burglary tools, narcotics, and a violation of felony probation.

On January 26, two patrol officers received a stolen vehicle Flock notification. They located the occupied stolen vehicle pulling into a parking lot. They apprehended the occupants and retrieved a handgun from the glove compartment. The occupants were validated gang members from a neighboring jurisdiction.

On December 11, 2023, officers were dispatched to the report of a stolen vehicle at a hotel. The victims vehicle was tracked using GPS and Flock ALPR cameras in the area. Officers observed a suspicious male running from the area where the vehicle was supposed to be. Officers detained the male and located the unoccupied, stolen vehicle. After identifying the suspect, it was discovered that he had been arrested a week prior for another stolen vehicle and was released on SORP (Supervised Own Recognizance Program). The suspect was transported to the Santa Clara County Main Jail and booked for possession of a stolen vehicle, felony evasion and possession of a controlled substance.

On December 14, 2023, the departments helicopter responded to a Flock hit for a stolen minivan. The departments helicopter tracked the vehicle until it parked in a wooded area. The two occupants fled from the vehicle and the aircrew guided patrol units to them. The driver and passenger suspects were taken into custody without incident. The driver had an outstanding no-bail felony warrant for his arrest. Additionally, several mail/shipping packages were located in the back of the van from multiple residential locations throughout the city.

On December 15, 2023, the departments helicopter responded to a patrol officer requesting assistance for a vehicle that was driving at a high rate of speed. The departments helicopter went overhead and picked up the vehicle. The officer moved up and attempted a vehicle stop on the freeway. The vehicle fled and the officer did not pursue. The departments helicopter broadcasted updates viewed from overhead of the suspects driving recklessly throughout San Jose, narrowly avoiding several collisions. Officers trailed at a distance out of view until the suspect vehicle stopped. Four suspects fled on foot and all four were apprehended shortly after.

On December 29, 2023, Officers were investigating a Flock hit for a stolen vehicle and found it unoccupied in a parking lot. The Officers surveilled the vehicle and within minutes, two suspects entered the vehicle and were detained. The driver fled on foot and was apprehended after a foot pursuit armed with a loaded 9mm ghost gun in his waistband. He was booked into jail for several felonies.

On November 12, 2023, the departments helicopter was monitoring Flock and responded to an alert in District Charles for a stolen vehicle. The helicopter located the occupied stolen vehicle and tracked it while patrol units responded. The suspect vehicle began driving recklessly and ran red lights upon seeing marked patrol vehicles. The helicopter tracked the suspect vehicle while patrol followed at a distance. The suspect vehicle drove into District Lincoln where it left the roadway into Coyote Creek. The two occupants fled into the creek and hid under brush. The helicopter maintained constant visual of the suspects while setting containment and guiding a contact team to the hiding suspects. Both were then contacted and taken into custody without incident.

On November 27, 2023, a carjacking at gunpoint occurred in a parking lot of a business. During the investigation, Flock cameras observed the stolen vehicle at several locations within the city. The suspect vehicle was located 90 minutes later. Officers attempted to conduct an enforcement stop, but the vehicle fled. Three officers initiated a vehicle pursuit due to the violent nature of the crime, the involvement of a firearm and the ongoing threat to the public. After three minutes, the vehicle pulled over and officers initiated a felony vehicle stop. The vehicle fled again, and the pursuit was re-initiated. The pursuit ended one minute later as the suspect exited the vehicle and fled on foot, where he was subsequently apprehended after a short foot pursuit. The suspect, a seventeen-year-old juvenile, was arrested in possession of a replica firearm.

On November 27, 2023, the departments helicopter located an occupied stolen vehicle. A high-risk car stop was attempted, and the vehicle fled. The helicopter followed the vehicle until the suspect parked and fled on foot while jumping fences. Inside the vehicle, numerous rounds of live ammunition were located. The suspect was apprehended by perimeter units as he attempted to break the perimeter. The suspect was observed discarding a backpack, which was recovered and contained a replica firearm and more live ammunition. The suspect was booked into jail for possession of a stolen vehicle with prior convictions, evading a peace officer, felon in possession of ammunition, violation of probation, possession of narcotics, and possession of narcotic paraphernalia.

On November 27, 2023, the departments helicopter was on patrol and responded to a Flock alert in District Robert for a stolen vehicle. The helicopter located the vehicle and tracked it while units responded to attempt a stop. Officers attempted a vehicle stop but the suspect failed to yield and fled. The helicopter tracked the suspect as he drove offroad into a park, ultimately abandoning his vehicle and fleeing on foot into a wooded area. Due to the difficult terrain and obstacles, officers were not able to pursue on foot. The suspect entered a dense foliage patch at the waters edge and attempted to hide. The suspect refused to follow officers commands, armed himself with a stick, and reached behind his waistband numerous times. Officers deployed a less lethal impact weapon but the suspect went deeper into the brush and disappeared from their view. The helicopter guided officers to the suspects location and they took him into custody. The suspect was found to have two felony warrants out of SJ and two misdemeanor warrants for intimate partner violence, assault with a deadly weapon, rape, and other serious crimes.

On September xx, 2023 AIR3 was on a patrol flight and located an occupied stolen vehicle via a Flock hit. The suspect vehicle appeared to notice AIR3 was overhead and quickly parked in a residential area where the driver and passenger fled from the vehicle on foot. AIR3 coordinated with responding officers to capture the suspects. The driver was booked for possession of a stolen vehicle, resisting arrest, possession of stolen property, and narcotics related charges. The passenger was booked for two outstanding felony warrants.

On September 24, 2023 AIR3 notified Patrol Officers of a Flock ALPR hit related to an occupied stolen vehicle driving in San Jose. AIR3 maintained a visual of the suspect vehicle until patrol officers were able to attempt a vehicle stop. The suspect vehicle failed to yield to Officers and a pursuit was not initiated. In coordination with AIR3, patrol Officers located the suspect vehicle after the suspect parked and fled on foot into the city of Campbell. Patrol officers responded to the suspects location and were ultimately able to apprehend the suspect without incident. The suspect was booked into jail for evading Officers, possession of a stolen vehicle, possession of burglary tools, and an out of county arrest warrant.

On September 25, 2023, a partial plate was obtained for a hit and run incident. Dispatch found a Flock hit that matched the vehicle description by using this partial plate. Patrol officers were sent to the registered owners address and took the suspect into custody.

On September 10, 2023, AIR3 located a stolen vehicle it was alerted to via the Flock ALPR system. The vehicle occupants observed AIR3 and the five occupants fled the vehicle on-foot prior to ground units arriving. Special Operations and Patrol ground units, with assistance from AIR3, were able to locate and arrest four of the five vehicle occupants, all of which were juveniles. The juveniles are suspects in approximately 60 vehicle break ins. The juveniles were booked into Juvenile Hall for multiple on-view charges and the stolen vehicle was impounded.

colonial-beach-va-pd:
Automated License Plate Readers (ALPRs)
427.1 VERSION
Review Date Effective Date Approving Authority Revised Date
12/1/23 05/11/2023 Les J. Parsons, Chief of

Police

12/9/24

427.2 PURPOSE AND SCOPE
The purpose of this policy is to provide guidance for the capture, storage and use of digital data
obtained through the use of Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) technology.
427.3 POLICY
The policy of the Colonial Beach Police Department is to utilize ALPR technology to capture and
store digital license plate data and images while recognizing the established privacy rights of the
public.
All data and images gathered by the ALPR are for the official use of this department. Because
such data may contain confidential information, it is not open to public review.
427.4 ADMINISTRATION
The ALPR technology, also known as License Plate Recognition (LPR), allows for the automated
detection of license plates. It is used by the Colonial Beach Police Department to convert data
associated with vehicle license plates for official law enforcement purposes, including identifying
stolen or wanted vehicles, stolen license plates and missing persons. It may also be used to
gather information related to active warrants, homeland security, electronic surveillance, suspect
interdiction and stolen property recovery.
All installation and maintenance of ALPR equipment, as well as ALPR data retention and access,
shall be managed by the Patrol Operations Commander. The Patrol Operations Commander will
assign members under his/her command to administer the day-to-day operation of the ALPR
equipment and data.
427.5 OPERATIONS
Use of an ALPR is restricted to the purposes outlined below. Department members shall not use,
or allow others to use, the equipment or database records for any unauthorized purpose.
(a) An ALPR shall only be used for official law enforcement business.
(b) An ALPR may be used in conjunction with any routine patrol operation or criminal
investigation. Reasonable suspicion or probable cause is not required before using
an ALPR.
(c) While an ALPR may be used to canvass license plates around any crime scene,
particular consideration should be given to using ALPR-equipped vehicles to canvass
areas around homicides, shootings and other major incidents. Partial license plates
reported during major crimes should be entered into the ALPR system in an attempt
to identify suspect vehicles.
(d) No member of this department shall operate ALPR equipment or access ALPR data
without first completing department-approved training.
(e) No ALPR operator may access confidential department, state or federal data unless
authorized to do so.
(f) If practicable, the officer should verify an ALPR response through the appropriate
official law enforcement database before taking enforcement action that is based
solely on an ALPR alert.

427.6 DATA COLLECTION AND RETENTION
The Patrol Operations Commander is responsible for ensuring systems and processes are in
place for the proper collection and retention of ALPR data. Data will be transferred from vehicles
to the designated storage in accordance with department procedures.
All stored ALPR data should be retained in accordance with the established records retention
schedule. Thereafter, ALPR data should be purged unless it has become, or it is reasonable to
believe it will become, evidence in a criminal or civil action or is subject to a discovery request
or other lawful action to produce records. In those circumstances, the applicable data should be
downloaded onto portable media and booked into evidence.
427.7 ACCOUNTABILITY
All data will be closely safeguarded and protected by both procedural and technological means.
The Colonial Beach Police Department will observe the following safeguards regarding access
to and use of stored data:
(a) All ALPR data downloaded to the mobile workstation and in storage shall be accessible
only through a login/password-protected system capable of documenting all access
of information by name, date and time.
(b) Members approved to access ALPR data under these guidelines are permitted to
access the data for legitimate law enforcement purposes only, such as when the data
relate to a specific criminal investigation or department-related civil or administrative
action.
(c) ALPR system audits should be conducted on a regular basis.
427.8 RELEASING ALPR DATA
The ALPR data may be shared only with other law enforcement or prosecutorial agencies
for official law enforcement purposes or as otherwise permitted by law, using the following
procedures: (a) The agency makes a written request for the ALPR data that includes:
1. The name of the agency.
2. The name of the person requesting.
3. The intended purpose of obtaining the information.
(b) The request is reviewed by the Patrol Operations Commander.
(c) The approved request is retained on file.
Requests for ALPR data by non-law enforcement or non-prosecutorial agencies will be processed
as provided in the Records Maintenance and Release Policy.

column1: Agency ALPR Policy
barrow-county-ga-so:
Agency ALPR Policy: The Sheriffs Office utilizes Flock Safety cameras located throughout the county of Barrow County. Flock Safety cameras are automated license plate readers. They are another form of investigative tool and can also be used for traffic enforcement. If the cameras are not functioning properly the deputy will notify the proper chain of command.

I. Deputies will log into Flock at the beginning of their shifts and log out at the end of shift.

II. The Flock camera system will only be used for law enforcement purposes. Deputies are prohibited from using Flock for personal reasons.

III. Any Hot List entries created by a deputy will be erased from the Hot List by said deputy once the entry is no longer needed.

IV. Deputies will have the following notifications always checked: Sex Offenders, Protection Order, Missing, Person, Violent Person, Warrants, Stolen Vehicle, Stolen Plate, Georgia DOR, and NCMEC Amber

column1: Ulta Beauty Burglary - Success story
blue-springs-mo-pd:
In this case, a suspect burglarized the Ulta Beauty store located in the Adams Dairy Landing shopping center, resulting in a loss exceeding $11,000. Through the use of Flock Safety License Plate Reader (LPR) cameras, officers and detectives were able to identify the suspect vehicle and obtain a license plate number.

As detectives and our crime analyst coordinated with Ulta Beauty Loss Prevention and partner agencies, the investigation ultimately linked the same suspect to 15 additional Ulta Beauty burglaries across six states. The combined total loss from these incidents was approximately $300,000. The investigative lead generated by the Flock LPR cameras was instrumental in identifying the suspect, leading to an arrest and the filing of criminal charges.

column1: Credit Card Skimming Ring - Success story
blue-springs-mo-pd:
In January 2024, a citizen reported that a credit card reader at a Hy-Vee gas station pump was hanging by wires. Officers determined that the device was not the original manufacturer-installed equipment, but rather a skimming device placed with the intent to unlawfully capture customers credit card information.

Patrol officers conducted checks at additional gas stations in the area and located several more skimming devices. While reviewing surveillance footage from one of the locations, officers identified a suspect vehicle; however, the license plate was not readable. By utilizing Flock Safety LPR cameras in the area, officers were able to identify the vehicle. This information led to the location of the vehicle and the execution of a search warrant at a related residence, where additional skimming equipment and computers were seized. The suspect was ultimately linked to additional crimes, formally charged, and the case was turned over to federal authorities for prosecution.

The Flock Safety LPR cameras deployed in Blue Springs have also assisted in numerous other investigations, including homicides, missing persons cases, thefts, and hit-and-run incidents. The examples outlined above represent just two instances demonstrating how the Blue Springs Police Department has effectively leveraged Flock Safety LPR technology to identify suspects, support investigations, and enhance public safety within our community.

Safe City Success Stories
casa-grande-az-pd:
The Casa Grande Police Department is committed to transparency, accountability, and the responsible use of technology. The Safe City Success Stories below provide real-world examples of how our Real Time Information Center (RTIC) and Flock Safety technologies are used to support investigations, locate missing persons, enhance officer safety, and protect our community. This section is updated regularly and displays recent activity to demonstrate the measurable impact of the Safe City Initiative.

These examples represent only a small snapshot of RTIC activity and outcomes and are not a comprehensive list of all cases or incidents where Safe City technology has assisted. Many uses occur daily and may not be included due to investigative sensitivity, case status, or the routine nature of the assistance provided.

column1: March 2026
casa-grande-az-pd:
A Gunshot Detection Alert led to the discovery of significant evidence of a shooting, including the discovery of bullet casings, which were entered into the National Integrated Ballistic Information Network to further the investigation.

RTIC utilized PTZ camera footage to assist in identifying and locating a shooting suspect from an incident that occurred in late February. Subsequently, the suspect was located and taken into custody.

LPR cameras were utilized to identify a stolen vehicle. DFR was utilized to track the vehicle returning to the city. RTIC communicated with patrol units, who were able to locate the stolen vehicle and arrest two suspects involved in the theft.

RTIC utilized DFR to respond to a burglary in progress. DFR observed a vehicle leaving the scene via an alleyway. RTIC communicated with responding officers, assisting them with furthering the investigation. Subsequently, one juvenile and one adult were arrested.

RTIC utilized LPR and DFR to search for and locate the suspect vehicle of a hit-and-run collision. One DFR responded to the residence of the registered owner of the suspect vehicle while the other kept a visual on the nearest intersections close to the LPR hits. Subsequently, patrol was able to locate the suspect vehicle and arrest the driver for an active warrant and leaving the scene of a collision.

RTIC utilized DFR to respond to a residential subdivision regarding a vehicle pursuit. DFR was utilized to maintain a safe and secure scene while officers conducted their investigation. Subsequently, one subject was arrested for unlawful flight from law enforcement, failing to obey a traffic control device, and DUI. A second subject was arrested for an active arrest warrant.

RTIC utilized DFR to respond to the call of an aggravated assault at a local business. Although the armed suspect fled the area, witness provided significant information
including the suspect license plate number. RTIC staff utilized DFR, PTZ, and LPR cameras to follow the suspect vehicle to a residence where patrol officers were able to take the suspect into custody without further incident.

column1: February 2026
casa-grande-az-pd:
RTIC identified and located a suspect vehicle involved in a pedestrian hit-and-run. Real-time intelligence provided to officers resulted in the suspect being located and the case resolved.

A reported stolen license plate was entered into the system, allowing partner agencies to receive alerts. An agency in Flagstaff identified the vehicle in their community, assisting the case officer's investigation.

RTIC supported the activation of Gunshot Detection technology, which led to the discovery of significant evidence related to weapons violations. Officers collected cartridge casings that were entered into evidence and analyzed for potential connections to other crimes.

RTIC assisted in locating another missing elderly individual who had left home in a vehicle. The individual was located using LPR cameras and safely reunited with family members.

RTIC staff utilized PTZ and LPR cameras to identify, track, and locate a suspect and their vehicle involved in a shooting that occurred in the downtown area. The license plate of the vehicle was entered as a FLOCK ALERT. Subsequently, a neighboring agency located the vehicle and arrested the driver for driving under the influence. This interaction aided the investigation and led to the identification of the shooter.

Drone First Responder (DFR) was utilized to locate a fleeing aggravated assault suspect. The suspect ran several blocks from the scene of the crime, navigating his way through multiple neighborhoods and backyards. RTIC staff located him with DFR and relayed real-time intelligence to the officers who were searching on foot. This led directly to the apprehension and arrest of the suspect.

RTIC utilized PTZ cameras to investigate a motorcycle versus vehicle collision that resulted in the motorcyclist sustaining serious injuries. The camera footage provided significant evidence (which would not have been identified otherwise) to further the investigation.

column1: January 2026
casa-grande-az-pd:
RTIC staff utilized PTZ and LPR cameras to identify, track, and locate a suspect vehicle involved in a theft of personal property from a local grocery store. Information was provided to the case officer, leading to the identification and arrest of the suspect.

Previously recorded PTZ camera footage was used to identify a suspect vehicle that followed a victim from a local bank after the victim used an ATM. The victim's vehicle was burglarized and money was stolen. This crime trend is commonly referred to as jugging.

PTZ and LPR cameras were used to establish a travel pattern for a vehicle associated with an individual who had an active felony warrant for weapons- related offenses.

When a panic alarm was activated at a local school, RTIC staff used PTZ cameras to monitor entry and exit points. This allowed real-time intelligence to be provided to responding officers before their arrival.

RTIC assisted in locating a missing elderly individual who had left home in a vehicle. The individual was located using LPR cameras and safely reunited with family members.

PTZ cameras were used to identify a group of juveniles at a local park who had purchased vaping products (e-cigarettes) from an individual in a vehicle. The vehicle was identified to further the investigation.

RTIC assisted in identifying a suspect vehicle involved in a pedestrian traffic collision. The vehicle left the scene, but partial license plate information and a witness description helped officers advance the investigation.

During a bank burglary alarm call, PTZ cameras were used to monitor exterior entry and exit points. RTIC staff provided real-time intelligence to responding officers prior to their arrival.

RTIC observed suspicious activity at the City's public library consistent with drug sales. Officers were dispatched, resulting in the arrest of two individuals for multiple crimes and an active warrant.

RTIC assisted in locating a vehicle associated with a domestic violence aggravated assault at a local apartment complex. Travel data indicated the suspect had left the city and was later returning toward the scene where the victim lived. Based on real-time intelligence, officers intercepted the vehicle and took the suspect into custody.

RTIC identified a suspect vehicle involved in a second reported jugging incident, in which a victim's vehicle was burglarized after the victim was followed from an ATM. This case remains an active investigation.

Additional Notable Successes  January 2026

RTIC also assisted with the following:
- Identification of a theft suspect within three minutes of the crime being reported; stolen property was recovered and returned to the owner.
- Identification of a vehicle involved in a robbery.
- Observation of suspicious activity in the downtown public library parking lot, resulting in the arrest of a subject with a U.S. Marshals Service warrant.
- Remote monitoring of a protest at City Hall, reducing the need for an on-site police presence and helping prevent potential escalation.
- Review of recorded footage showing a City employee assisting an individual who had fallen near railroad tracks, allowing the employee's positive actions to be recognized.

city-of-peoria-pd:
Peoria Police Officers responded to a local city park after a caller reported multiple males arguing. During the dispute, one male pulled a gun and pointed it at the others and the caller. He then fled in a gold Chevrolet Equinox. Shortly after, another male involved called to report that the suspect in the Equinox had fired multiple shots.

Peoria Police Real Time Crime Center (RTCC) detectives acted immediately. Using Flock data and traffic cameras, they located the suspect vehicle leaving the scene and created a "hotlist." Another Flock alert indicated the vehicle was returning to the shooting area. RTCC monitored cameras and directed officers to its last known location. Within minutes, officers found the vehicle and the suspect in a residential area. The male was taken into custody without incident, and the firearm was recovered.
__________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
On 02/26/26 SIU detective hot-listed the suspect vehicle using the Flock system. Numerous alerts were received during the early morning hours. Detectives started actively looking for the suspect vehicle again at about 1008 hours. Another Flock alert was received in the area of 8400 W Bell Rd heading westbound. A Detective with SIU immediately got on the traffic cameras and started following the vehicle while receiving more Flock alerts. Coordination with North Patrol started, and the suspect was located by North Patrol at the Walgreens at 91st Ave and Union Hills. The suspect was arrested without incident and booked on numerous felony charges.

column1: Solved Stories
city-of-peoria-pd:
MISSING ENDANGERED MALE LOCATED

The Peoria Police Department recently responded to a missing/endangered person call involving a 79-year-old male suffering from Alzheimer's disease who left his family's apartment complex while driving a white Hyundai Elantra that was low on fuel.

RTCC Detectives immediately acted on this information and entered the vehicle's license plate into the Flock Safety LPR System as a hot listed vehicle. Shortly after, the vehicle was detected near Union Hills Drive and the New River Trail.

As the individual continued traveling through the Valley, RTCC Detectives received multiple Flock notifications documenting the vehicle's movement through Surprise and Sun City. These real-time alerts proved instrumental in tracking the vehicle's path and maintaining situational awareness as the incident rapidly escalated toward a potential Silver Alert.

Later, Peoria RTCC Detectives received another Flock notification placing the vehicle in the Verrado area. They coordinated with the Buckeye Police Department, which had officers in the area and was able to locate the vehicle and successfully conduct a traffic stop.

Officers coordinated with the family and transported a family member to the scene, where the individual was safely reunited with loved ones. Based on the locations reported, it is estimated he drove at over 150 miles. This incident was close to becoming a Silver Alert. However, due to the effective teamwork of Dispatch, Patrol Officers, RTCC Detectives, and the Valley-wide Flock network, the individual was located quickly, safely, and returned home.

__________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________

On August 25th, 2025, the Peoria Police Department's Real-Time Crime Center (RTCC) played a crucial role in reuniting a missing 85-year-old woman with her family after she failed to arrive at her intended destination. Utilizing Flock LPR and other technology systems, the RTCC quickly tracked her vehicle's movements and directed patrol officers to her location. This effective collaboration between the RTCC, dispatch, and patrol teams ensured a safe and successful outcome. We are proud to see how passion, pride, and purpose continue to make a real difference in our community.
__________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
The Peoria Police Department's Real Time Crime Center (RTCC) utilized Flock license plate recognition (LPR) technology to research and identify critical information that helped advance a major vehicle burglary investigation.

Flock technology played a pivotal role in identifying two suspect vehicles connected to a series of vehicle burglaries in the residential area near 107th Ave and Happy Valley Rd.

The RTCC reviewed data from Flock and traffic camera footage for the initial detection, which was then provided to detectives for further investigation. Using this information, the detectives were able to gather additional evidence linking three co-conspirators to the vehicles used to commit the burglaries.

The investigation evolved into a coordinated, multi-jurisdictional operation involving seven search warrants--five residential and two vehicles. This collaborative effort resulted in the arrest of two suspects and the recovery of key evidence, including firearms and suspect clothing.
__________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
In August of 2025, Flock license plate recognition (LPR) technology played a crucial role in identifying a suspect involved in multiple felony shoplifting and organized retail theft cases in Peoria. Using Flock data, investigators determined the vehicle used in several incidents and confirmed the associated Nevada license plate through matching descriptions and witness photos.

Further investigation revealed that the exact vehicle and suspect were linked to similar crimes in other jurisdictions. Collaboration with those agencies confirmed the suspect's identity and activities, showing that he had traveled from Nevada to Arizona while on probation to commit the offenses.

Through coordination between agencies, the suspect was later arrested in Nevada for related crimes. This case demonstrates how Flock technology enhances investigative capabilities, supports interagency communication, and helps law enforcement identify and locate suspects across state lines.
__________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
In September of 2025, detectives investigated a case involving a suspect who violated an active Order of Protection by repeatedly contacting and following the protected individual in violation of court orders.

During the investigation, detectives used Flock license plate recognition (LPR) technology to gather supporting evidence related to the suspect's vehicle and its connection to reported incidents. Flock data helped verify key details in the case and corroborate information obtained from other investigative sources, including GPS records from Adult Probation and law enforcement databases.

The combined evidence established probable cause for Aggravated Harassment, leading to the suspect's arrest on multiple felony and misdemeanor charges. The suspect was booked and held without bond.

This case highlights how Flock LPR technology supports investigations by providing reliable information, strengthening cases, and enhancing victim safety.

__________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________
In October of 2025, Peoria Police responded to a road rage incident near 91st Avenue and Peoria Avenue, where a female victim was shot in the leg. The Real Time Crime Center (RTCC) quickly analyzed data from the Flock license plate recognition (LPR) system. It provided investigators with the vehicle and license plate driven by the shooter. This crucial information significantly reduced investigative time-saving countless hours of traditional police work that could have taken days to complete.

With the information provided by the RTCC and Flock, detectives identified the suspect, obtained a positive victim identification through a photo lineup, and secured search warrants for the suspect's vehicle and residence.

With the help of the Peoria PD Special Assignments Unit, investigators apprehended the suspect without incident at his residence in Phoenix. A firearm and a shell casing were recovered from the vehicle, and the suspect later confessed to the shooting.

This case highlights how the RTCC and Flock LPR technology enhance investigative efficiency, accelerate suspect identification, and strengthen public safety outcomes

column1: Succes Stories
clinton-ct-pd:
1. Disruption of Multi-State Organized Retail Crime Ring

(Case Reference: 2500005682 Date: April 7, 2025)

Impact on Town Safety: Directly dismantled a sophisticated criminal operation targeting our retail corridor and recovered high-value stolen property, protecting local businesses from economic loss.

Outcome Summary: Detectives utilized Flock LPR data to track a suspect vehicle involved in a major larceny at the Clinton Premium Outlets. The system tracked the vehicle from Clinton to Groton, CT, and finally to the Providence Place Mall in Rhode Island. Coordinating with regional partners, officers apprehended four suspects connected to a Venezuelan organized crime group and recovered over $9,000.00 in stolen merchandise.

2. Cross-State Life-Saving Intervention (Suicidal Person)

(Case Reference: 25-2453 Date: February 10, 2025)

Impact on Town Safety: Demonstrates the immense value of the "National Lookup" feature, showing how our local system connects with the broader investigative ecosystem to protect Clinton residents even when they are hundreds of miles away.

Outcome Summary: CPD officers were investigating the disappearance of a suicidal male who had left a note and transferred his assets. Because the system is connected to the national network, officers detected the individuals vehicle via a Flock camera hit in York, Maine. This critical intelligence allowed local authorities to locate him safely in Bath, Maine, facilitating immediate medical intervention.

3. Immediate Apprehension of Felony Offender & Fentanyl Seizure

(Case Reference: 2500007724 Date: May 19, 2025)

Impact on Town Safety: Removed a dangerous individual and illicit narcotics from the street, directly linking technology to the prevention of potential drug-related harm.

Outcome Summary: The Flock LPR system alerted officers to a stolen 2021 Volkswagen Tiguan traveling through Clinton. Officers quickly located and stopped the vehicle on East Main Street. The stop resulted in the arrest of the operator for possession of a stolen vehicle and the seizure of cocaine and fentanyl, along with drug paraphernalia.

4. Fugitive Arrest: Subject with 10 Outstanding Warrants

(Case Reference: 2500008456 Date: June 3, 2025)

Impact on Town Safety: Proves the systems ability to act as a force multiplier, helping officers identify dangerous individuals hiding in public spaces before they can re-offend.

Outcome Summary: An alert for a stolen vehicle entering the Clinton Crossing Outlets led officers to the vehicle's location. Officers subsequently located the operator inside a retail store. A records check revealed he had ten total outstanding arrest warrants from various agencies. The arrest also resulted in the recovery of over $5,000.00 in stolen valuables.

5. Safe Recovery of High-Risk Missing Person (Silver Alert)

(Case Reference: 2500011556 Date: August 13, 2025)

Impact on Town Safety: Highlights the networks critical role in protecting vulnerable populations, such as the elderly or those suffering from dementia.

Outcome Summary: Officers responded to a report of a missing person with dementia who was feared lost. A Silver Alert was issued. Flock LPR technology tracked the vehicle from Fairfield County and provided a real-time alert at approximately 21:30 hours placing the vehicle in Madison. This allowed CPD to coordinate with Madison PD and the Connecticut State Police to safely recover the individual in Sturbridge, MA.

6. Residential Burglary and Vehicle Theft Investigation

(Case Reference: 2500014160 Date: October 12, 2025)

Impact on Town Safety: Provided forensic-level evidence for a serious residential crime, offering peace of mind to victims that the department has the tools to solve crimes occurring in neighborhoods.

Outcome Summary: Following a burglary and motor vehicle theft at a residence on Old Mill Road, detectives utilized Flock LPR data to identify the travel patterns and specific timeline of the stolen vehicle. This data confirmed movement patterns seen on private surveillance, significantly narrowing the investigative timeline and supporting the recovery effort.

7. Solving Local Property Crime: Bicycle Theft Recovery

(Case Reference: 25000010144 Date: July 20, 2025)

Impact on Town Safety: Underscores that the system is not just for major felonies but is also a vital tool for community policing, helping to solve property crimes that affect the daily quality of life for residents.

Outcome Summary: Officers investigated the theft of a bicycle, a crime often difficult to solve due to a lack of physical evidence. Investigators linked a suspect vehicle to the theft and entered it into the Flock system. A short time later, an alert notified patrol officers of the vehicle's location. The vehicle was intercepted, the operator admitted to the theft, and the stolen bicycle was recovered and returned to its owner.

8. Arrest of Evading Driver in Hit-and-Run

(Case Reference: 2500003052 Date: March 2, 2025)

Impact on Town Safety: Ensures accountability in hit-and-run incidents, sending a message that fleeing from an accident in Clinton will result in identification and prosecution.

Outcome Summary: Following a motor vehicle crash on North High Street where one vehicle fled the scene, Dispatch utilized Flock LPR data to determine the evading vehicle had entered the Clinton Crossing Outlets. Officers were guided to the location, found the vehicle, and arrested the operator for Evading Responsibility and other charges.

9. Inter-Agency Assist: Fraud and Larceny Arrests

(Case Reference: 2500012228 Date: August 27, 2025)

Impact on Town Safety: Illustrates the "force multiplier" effect of sharing data with neighboring towns to stop traveling criminals.

Outcome Summary: The Madison Police Department issued a BOLO (Be On the Lookout) for a suspect vehicle involved in attempted larceny and check fraud. A Flock camera in Clinton flagged the vehicle entering town. CPD officers intercepted the vehicle and detained the occupants, who were subsequently taken into custody and charged by Madison PD, preventing potential fraud in Clinton.

10. Proactive Stolen Vehicle Interdiction

(Case Reference: 2500012938 Date: September 14, 2025)

Impact on Town Safety: Prevents crimes before they happen by intercepting stolen vehicles, which are often used to commit secondary offenses like robbery or shoplifting.

Outcome Summary: Flock cameras alerted officers to a stolen Chrysler Town & Country entering Clinton. Officers located and stopped the vehicle on East Main Street. The operator was arrested for possession of a stolen vehicle, removing a liability from the roadways and returning property to its rightful owner.

Based on the success stories documented in the provided reports, here is the drafted success story for the January 10th incident.

11. Proactive Larceny and Trespass Arrest

(Date: January 10, 2026)

Impact on Town Safety: This case highlights the system's role in enforcing court orders and preventing repeat offenses. By proactively identifying a known offender prohibited from a high-traffic commercial area, officers prevented further economic loss to local businesses and reinforced community safety standards.

Outcome Summary: On January 10th, the Clinton Police Department received a Flock LPR alert for a vehicle entering town that was linked to previous shoplifting arrests at the Clinton Premium Outlets. Officers located the vehicle, which was parked away from the immediate retail area in an apparent attempt to avoid detection. Officers set up surveillance and monitored the vehicle until the operator returned. column1: Corinth PD Automated License Plate Reader Policy
corinth-tx-pd:
I. PURPOSE
The purpose of this policy is to establish the guidelines for the proper use of the ALPR by the members of the Corinth Police Department while maintaining compliance with applicable state and federal laws.

II. POLICY
The Corinth Police Departments ALPR Policy defines a minimum set of guidelines to govern the use of ALPR Data to enable the collection and use of such data in a manner consistent with respect for an individuals privacy and civil liberties. Employees shall abide by the procedures outlined in this directive when using the ALPR systems, thereby increasing the efficiency and effectiveness of this department's public safety efforts in a
manner that also safeguards the privacy concerns of the general public.

III. DEFINITIONS
A. ALPR - is a generic acronym for Automated License Plate Recognition, Automated License Plate Reader, or License Plate Recognition (LPR). ALPR Systems can be implemented in multiple configurations: mobile (vehicle-mounted cameras), portable (stationary systems that are set up at a single point and moved when operations are complete), and fixed (cameras mounted to a fixed object such as a designated pole, traffic signal, light pole, highway overpass, etc.). The Corinth Police Department will only utilize the fixed camera option for all FLOCK cameras that are deployed.
B. Hotlist - A list of known license plates and vehicles of interest, which are stolen, wanted for, or potentially associated with unlawful activity or missing persons.
C. Read Record - A record of a plate that was read by ALPR that was not associated with any hotlist at the time it was captured.
D. Hit Record - A record of a plate that was read by ALPR that matched a plate number on a hotlist and generated an alert.
E. Hotlist Administrator  Authorized personnel whose duty is maintaining the ALPRs hotlist.
F. Confirmed ALPR Alert  A visual confirmation that the license plate matches the information captured by the ALPR and reported in the corresponding alert to include the correct state of origin. The license plate information is confirmed with the National and Texas Crime Information Centers (NCIC/TCIC) when applicable.
G. Hotlist Alert Categories - This is a list of the offense categories that will trigger a hotlist alert:
1. Amber Alert
2. Armed Robbery
3. Assault
4. Attempt to Locate
5. BOLO
6. Capias Warrant
7. Felony Warrant
8. Fugitive
9. Gang or Suspected Terrorist
10. Hit and Run
11. Homicide
12. Law Enforcement Suspect
13. Misdemeanor
14. Missing Person
15. Narcotics
16. Protection Order
17. Reported Lost/Missing
18. Stolen License Plate
19. Stolen Vehicle
20. Suspect
21. Threats to Law Enforcement
22. Violent Person
23. Wanted Person
24. Wanted Vehicle
25. Warrants

IV. PROCEDURES
A. Use of Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) Equipment
1. The ALPR systems are the property of the City of Corinth. Officers use of ALPR equipment is restricted to public safety related missions of the department.
Department members shall not use, or allow others to use, the equipment or database records for any unauthorized purpose.
a. Appropriate use for the ALPR system includes, but are not limited to:
i. Identifying stolen or wanted vehicles, stolen license plates, and missing persons.
ii. Locate and apprehend individuals subject to active arrest warrants or
otherwise lawfully sought by law enforcement.
iii. Locate witnesses and victims of crime.
iv. Locate missing and elderly individuals, including responding to any
state or local issued alerts.
v. Support local, state, federal and tribal public safety departments in the
identification of vehicles associated with targets of criminal
investigations, including investigations of serial crimes.
2. The ALPR may be used for other than patrol functions, when authorized by the Chief of Police, when articulable information exists to establish sufficient facts to give an Authorized User reasonable suspicion to believe that a particular individual, entity, or vehicle may be involved in definable criminal activity.
3. ALPR may be used to canvass license plates in a public area around any crime scene. Partial license plates reported during major crimes can be entered into the ALPR system to help identify suspect vehicles.
4. Officers who conduct a law enforcement action based on a Confirmed ALPR Alert will consider the level of risk associated with the nature of the offense and ensure that their response complies with all applicable statutes, City, and department policies.
5. Unless authorized by the Chief of Police, ALPR will not be utilized in any vehicle that is not identifiable as a Corinth Police Department vehicle.

B. Prohibited Use
Use of an ALPR is restricted to the purposes outlined below.
1. Except when done pursuant to a court order or exigent circumstances, it is a violation to utilize the ALPR to record license plates out of public view where there is a reasonable expectation of privacy.
2. It is a violation to use the ALPR systems and its associated data to harass or
improperly intimidate any individual or group.
3. The ALPR systems and associated data shall not be used solely to target an individual or group based on race, gender, religion, political affiliation, nationality, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or disability.
4. No ALPR operator may access confidential department, state, or federal data unless authorized.
5. The ALPR system and any associated data shall not be used for personal reasons and are only authorized for legitimate law enforcement purpose.
6. The ALPR system shall not be used for any Class C misdemeanor related offenses.

C. Data Security, Access, and Accountability
1. Only authorized personnel shall have access to ALPR data.
2. The Professional Standard section will audit ALPR searches every six months and prepare a report for the Chief of Police.
3. ALPR data shall be kept in a secure data storage system with access restricted to authorized users. This information is considered confidential to the extent permitted by law.
4. ALPR systems, associated equipment, and databases are authorized for official public safety purposes. Personnel who misuse this equipment and associated databases or data may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including termination of employment.
5. ALPR systems, ALPR data, and associated media are the property of this agency and intended for use in conducting official law enforcement business.
6. Officers may only access stored data to perform a legitimate law enforcement function. Officers shall include the incident report number or call for service number, if available.
7. Designated personnel shall check equipment regularly to ensure functionality and camera alignment. Any equipment that falls outside expected functionality shall be reported immediately to the Field Operations Commander.

D. Storage and Retention
1. The Corinth Police Department is submitting reads through FLOCK Safety directly to DPS. We send reads back to DPS every 24 hours and retain the data for 30 days.
2. Hits shall be retained no longer than necessary for legitimate law enforcement
purposes.
3. If a hotlist attachment is made to the system, it shall be the responsibility of the Hotlist Administrator to include an expiration date for the attachment in the system.
If the hot list attachment is no longer needed before it is due to expire, the Hotlist Administrator shall immediately remove the hit from the system manually.

V. FLOCK CAMERA LOCATIONS

A. These are the current approved locations for FLOCK cameras:
1. S/B Post Oak Dr. @ S/B IH35E SR
2. E/B Shady Shores Rd. @ Lakeview Blvd.
3. W/B Lake Sharon @ S/B IH35E SR
4. N/B Oakmont @ FM 2181
5. N/B Post Oak Dr. @ FM 2181
6. N/B Parkridge Dr. @ FM 2181
7. N/B South Garrison Rd. @ FM 2181

9. E/B Corinth Pkwy @ N/B IH35E SR
10. S/B Corinth Pkwy @ S/B IH35E SR
11. W/B Meadowview Dr. @ S/B IH35E SR
12. N/B FM 2499 @ South City Limits
13. E/B Lake Sharon Dr. @ FM 2499
14. E/B Robinson Rd. @ Pine Hills Ln.
15. N/B IH35E SR @ FM 2181
16. W/B FM 2181 @ S/B IH35E SR
17. S/B IH35E SR @ POST OAK Dr.
18. Corinth Commons at AGORA Community Park (Condor)

VI. EFFECTIVE DATE
A. Any previous directive, rule, order or regulation that pertains to this subject matter and its amendments shall remain in full force and effect for any violation(s) which occur prior to the effective date of this General Order.
B. If any section, sentence, clause or phrase of this General Order is, for any reason, held to be invalid, such decision shall not affect the validity of the remaining portions of this General Order.
C. All training on this General Order will be in accordance with General Order 100, Written Directive System, Chapter VIII, Training.
D. The effective date is stated in the header block of this General Order.
